source_record.common_cost_and_alternative: Admission delay, long-lead exceptions, item definition and hidden backlog count. Naturally bounded low-volume work can use finish-before-start and a brief exception note.
attempted_contrary_interfaces: First-tier diversity treated as independent lower-tier supply.
A complete document treated as operational capability.
A partial exposure or criterion input rejected for failing the whole receiver.
Capacity, stock or staff double-counted for routine and contingency use.
Buyer savings treated as joint fair gain.

positive_controls.argument: An actual admission limit and its exception behavior supply a timing/loading condition that the shared interface contract must represent; otherwise individually compatible components can disagree about accepted work or overload response.
A genuine release limit bounds the number of active commitments before the next relevant result, supplying a partial exposure bound to the staging decision when those items carry that commitment.

The real cap, work definition, upstream backlog and exception policy constrain the forecast model and prevent interpreting a reduced admitted-cycle-time statistic as improvement of total demand completion.
The actual release boundary and long-lead exceptions expose when supplier work may begin and which commitment would be delayed, supplying a concrete coordination premise.
A demonstrated cap on concurrent relevant changes bounds one operational workload or exposed transition population, which can inform support and rehearsal readiness.
The number and identity of active commitments can bound the work requiring reconciliation or restoration, a partial input to the recovery estimate.
An enforced active-maintenance boundary and visible backlog reveal committed support work and prevent treating unchecked additions as already supportable.
A demonstrated admission bound supplies one exposure or capacity condition for proportional control selection while leaving propagation, legal obligations and recovery separate.
